artworks.title: Neoptolemus Slays Eurypylus (Attic black-figure amphora)
artworks.description: Shoulder of Martin-von-Wagner-Museum L 309 (from Vulci): Neoptolemus has cut down Eurypylus and pursues the charioteer until Apollo steps in with the bow. The Mysian son of Telephus — Troy's late ally from the Little Iliad cycle — dies in black-figure before Achilles' son.

popCulture.title: Little Iliad
popCulture.creator: Lesches (attrib.)
popCulture.description: Epic Cycle fragment tradition: Eurypylus arrives from Mysia with the Ceteians and falls to Neoptolemus — Telephus' son as Troy's last great reinforcement.

popCulture.title: Eurypylus (son of Telephus)
popCulture.description: King of Mysia who fought for Troy and was slain by Neoptolemus — distinct from Homeric Eurypylus son of Euaemon.
